data.text: Eventual consistency means data will converge to the same value over time, without guaranteeing immediate consistency. It enables highly available systems.

terms.definition: Data converges to the same value given enough time.
Storing state as a sequence of events.
Command Query Responsibility Segregation: separate read and write models.
The process of data becoming consistent over time.

items: Event sourcing: store events, derive state
CQRS: separate read and write models

data.text: Event sourcing stores state as a sequence of events. Instead of storing the current state, you store the events that led to it. The current state is derived by replaying events.

CQRS separates the read model from the write model. Writes use one model optimized for updates. Reads use another model optimized for queries. The read model is eventually consistent with the write model.

data.caption: Eventual Consistency Flow
data.definition:
sequenceDiagram
    participant W as Write Service
    participant E as Event Bus
    participant R as Read Model
    W->>E: Publish Event
    E->>R: Deliver Event
    R->>R: Update Read Model
    Note over R: Eventually consistent
    participant Q as Query Service
    Q->>R: Query
    R-->>Q: Data (possibly stale)

data.title: Exercise: Design Eventual Consistency
data.expectedOutcome: A design with write model, events, and read model

data.title: Key Takeaways
data.takeaway: Eventual consistency trades immediacy for availability and scale.
